paper.title: Online Data Collection for Efficient Semiparametric Inference

settings.name_in_paper: Online Moment Selection (equal cost, known horizon)
unmapped: Arms are data sources (distributions over possibly different variable subsets); each query returns an i.i.d. sample from the chosen source

Objective is efficient estimation of a scalar target parameter identified by moment conditions (semiparametric GMM with nuisance parameters); regret is asymptotic MSE of the estimator minus that of the oracle fixed allocation kappa*
Learner knows the moment conditions, the selection map m and the target function f_tar
settings.definition_quote: We represent the available data sources by $\DM := ( \PB^{(i)} )_{i=1}^{\CardC}$, a collection of probability distributions. Querying a data source $\PB^{(i)} \in \DM$ is equivalent to drawing an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) sample from $\PB^{(i)}$. ... We denote by $T$, the horizon or the known total number of queries the agent can make.

unmapped: Arms are data sources; objective is efficient semiparametric estimation of a target parameter; regret is asymptotic MSE relative to oracle allocation
Learner knows the moment conditions, the selection map m and the target function f_tar
settings.definition_quote: The $\epsilon$-greedy policy does not require the horizon $T$ to be specified in advance (unlike ETC and ETG, where the exploration depends on $T$).

unmapped: Each data source has a known per-query cost c_i > 0 and the learner has a known total budget B; horizon T is random
The learner knows the cost vector c
Objective is efficient semiparametric estimation; regret is asymptotic MSE (scaled by sqrt(B)) relative to oracle allocation
settings.definition_quote: We denote the (known) budget by $B \in \NB$ and the cost vector by $c \in \RB^{\CardC}_{>0}$, where $c_i$ is the cost of querying the data source $\PB^{(i)} \in \DM$. Due to the cost structure, the horizon $T$ is a random variable dependent on $\pi$ with $T = \max \{ t \in \NB : t (\kappa^\top_t c) \leq B  \}$.

conditions: policy satisfies the conditions of Prop. 2 (incl. kappa_T converges in probability)

source.label: prop:regret-is-non-negative
source.quote: Suppose that (i) $\widehat{\theta}_T$ is estimated using Eq.~\ref{eq:gmm-estimator-argmin}, (ii) Assumption~\ref{assump:kappa-star-identify} holds, and (iii) the conditions of Prop.~\ref{prop:asymp-normality} hold. Then, for any data collection policy $\pi$, $R_{\infty}(\pi) \geq 0$.

results.notes: Regret = asymptotic MSE of sqrt(T)(beta_hat - beta*) minus oracle variance V_*(kappa*); comparator is the oracle fixed allocation policy. Quantity mapped to other.

conditions: conditions of Prop. 2 (consistency/ULLN properties, Neyman orthogonality, second-order remainder o_p(t^{-1/2}), compact Theta, identification)
conditions of Lemma 2 (kappa* unique minimizer; derivatives satisfy ULLN property)
tuning: exploration fraction e = o(1) with T*e -> infinity (e.g. e = 1/sqrt(T))

source.label: thm:etc-regret
source.quote: Suppose that the conditions of Prop.~\ref{prop:asymp-normality} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:oracle-simplex-estimation} hold, and Assumption~\ref{assumption:exploration} holds. Then, $R_\infty(\pi_{\text{ETC}}) = 0$.

results.notes: Zero asymptotic regret (asymptotic MSE relative to oracle).

bound.regime: T -> infinity, finite number of rounds

tuning: batch size S with lim S/T = r in (0,1) (finite rounds)

source.label: thm:etg-finite-rounds
source.quote: Suppose that (i) the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:etc-regret} hold and (ii) (Finite rounds) $\lim_{T \to \infty} S / T = r$ for some constant $r \in (0, 1)$. Then, $R_\infty(\pi_{\text{ETG}}) = 0$.

bound.regime: T -> infinity, any batch size S

conditions: nuisance estimators strongly consistent: ||eta_hat - eta*|| -> 0 a.s.

source.label: thm:etg-infinite-rounds
source.quote: Suppose that (i) the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:etc-regret} hold and (ii) the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oracle-simplex-estimation-almost-sure} hold. Then, for any batch size $S$, $R_\infty(\pi_{\text{ETG}}) = 0$.

conditions: conditions of Lemma 3 (strongly consistent nuisance estimators)
tuning: (eps_t) non-increasing with E_T = sum eps_t = o(T) and E_T -> infinity (e.g. eps_t ~ 1/t)

source.label: thm:eps-greedy
source.quote: Let $(\epsilon_t)_{t=1}^{\infty}$ be a non-increasing sequence and $E_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} \epsilon_t$. Suppose that (i) the conditions of Prop.~\ref{prop:asymp-normality} hold; (ii) the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lemma:oracle-simplex-estimation-almost-sure} hold; and (iii) $E_T = o(T)$ and $E_T \to \infty$ (e.g., $\epsilon_t \asymp 1 / t$). Then, the $\epsilon$-greedy policy suffers zero regret: $R_\infty(\pi_{\epsilon\text{-greedy}}) = 0$.

results.notes: Paper states this policy does not need T in advance.

source.label: prop:regret-etc-cost-structure
source.quote: Suppose that the conditions of Prop.~\ref{prop:asymp-normality} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:oracle-simplex-estimation} hold. If $e = o(1)$ and $Be \rightarrow \infty$ as $B \to \infty$, then $R_{\infty}(\pi_{\text{ETC-CS}}) = 0$.

results.notes: Regret here uses sqrt(B) scaling and oracle V_*(kappa*)(kappa*^T c).

conditions: conditions of Prop. 2 and Lemma 3 (strongly consistent nuisance estimators)

source.label: prop:regret-etg-cs
source.quote: Suppose that the conditions of Prop.~\ref{prop:asymp-normality} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:oracle-simplex-estimation-almost-sure} hold. If $e = o(1)$ and $Be \to \infty$ as $B \to \infty$, then $R_\infty(\pi_{\text{ETG-CS}}) = 0$.
